koma.support_effect: 0 damage; afflicts opponents with the blind status effect
koma.quote: Neuro appears, quickly throws a brain a decent distance, and upon landing on the ground, purple gas to come out. 0 damage; afflicts opponents with the blind status effect

koma.support_effect: 0 damage; causes the invisible status effect
koma.quote: Neuro appears behind your character with his bird head form, spits out purple water out of his mouth, causing those that touch the water to become invisible. 0 damage; causes the invisible status effect

passives: Gain SP by attacking characters or defending against characters that have the opposite nature

specials.name: You, you are the killer!
specials.description: Yako suddenly appears with Neuro in his regular form right beside her. Yako and Neuro then point in the direction they are facing, causing a purple aura to come out of her fingertip in a straight, narrow fashion. It only goes a short distance (less than half the player's screen), and the aura never leaves her fingertip.
specials.damage: Power/Knowledge: 3 hits, 10 per hit, 30 total; Laughter: 3 hits, 15 per hit, 45 total
specials.quote: Yako and Neuro then point in the direction they are facing, causing a purple aura to come out of her fingertip in a straight, narrow fashion. Good move, but the 5-koma version is much better due to the fact that the aura travels a decent amount further that the 4-koma version.

specials.name: Ejiki
specials.description: A monster (in reality Shirota, the chef who injects himself with the doping soup in the middle of chapter 6) appears behind Neuro and charges at him. Neuro quickly dodges the charge and then Shirota jumps forward and slams down on the ground.
specials.quote: Honestly, this really isn't a good special. Too much lag from when you start the move to when it actually causes damage, and it can't be comboed into to anything else that well.

passives: Gain SP by attacking characters or defending against characters that have the opposite nature

specials.name: You, you are the killer!

specials.damage: Power/Knowledge: 3 hits, 10 per hit, 30 total; Laughter: 3 hits, 15 per hit, 45 total

specials.name: You, you are the killer!
specials.description: More or less the same as the 4-koma neutral X special, but the aura travels a good amount further and is much wider, making it easier to combo into.
specials.damage: Power/Knowledge: 5 hits, 5 damage per hit for four hits and 15 on the final hit, 35 total; Laughter: 5 hits, two hits for 7, two hits for 8, and 22 on the final hit, 52 total
specials.quote: More or less the same as his 4-koma neutral X special, but the aura travels a good amount further and is much wider, making it easier to combo into.

specials.name: Hitorikii
specials.description: Yako appears in an evening gown and starts singing. Anyone hit in the radius around Neuro while Yako is singing is afflicted with the Confusion status effect.
specials.quote: Yako appears in an evening gown and starts singing. Anyone who is hit in the radious around Neuro while Yako is singing is afflicted with the Confusion status effect. Cause no damage.

moves.name: Neutral B
moves.description: Neuro snaps his fingers, sending the opponent upward. A good combo starter or ring-out setup with his up-Y attack.
moves.quote: Neuro snaps his fingers, causing the opponent to be sent upwards in the air. A great move set up attack, Neuro's neutral B can easily start a combo, or to set up a possible ring out attack when followed with his up-Y attack.

moves.name: Forward B
moves.description: Neuro slips into his true form and fires a rifle at the opponent; not a great move, but chains easily into his forward Y.
moves.quote: Forward B: Neuro slips into his true from, while firing a rifle at the opponent. Not that great a move, but if the hit does connect, it can chain easily into his forward Y move.

moves.name: Up B
moves.description: Neuro turns his arm into a chainsaw, which can hit opponents on ledges above due to Neuro's height and the chainsaw's length. Leaves Neuro facing the opposite direction, making it a good combo-ender.
moves.damage: Power/Knowledge: 1 damage per hit, 10 in total; Laughter: 1-2 damage per hit, 15 in total
moves.quote: Up B: Neuro turns his arm into a chainsaw, which can easily hit opponents on ledges above, due to Neuro's height and the length of the chainsaw. This move also causes Neuro to end up facing in the opposite direction, which makes it best for the ending hit to a combo. (deals 10 hits in total)

moves.name: Down B
moves.description: Neuro causes a speech bubble to appear while asking a question; opponents hit by it are forced to switch characters, like all characters' down B attacks.
moves.quote: Down B: Neuro causes a speech bubble to appear while he is asking a question. Opponents hit by the speech bubble are forced to switch characters, if they have any other ones availible for use in thier current deck, like all character's down B attacks.

moves.name: Aerial B
moves.description: Neuro turns part of his hair into a three-pronged spear end. Not that great a move compared to his aerial Y, best used against opponents who spend most of their time evading.
moves.quote: Aerial B: Neuro turns part of his hair into a three-pronged spear end. Really not that great a move, especially compared to his excellent Aerial Y attack. Best used when hit opponents that spend most of thier time evading.

moves.name: Neutral Y
moves.description: Neuro swings Yako around like a club. One of his best moves: good damage, combos easily into his neutral X super and certain support koma, and knocks the opponent back a decent distance.
moves.quote: Neutral Y: Neuro swings Yako aroung like a club. One of his best moves, it causes a good amount of damage, can be easily comboed into his nuetral X super as well as certain support koma, and can send the opponent a decent ways back.

moves.name: Forward Y
moves.description: Neuro brings out Yako to have her hair try to cover the opponent; if the initial hit connects, the hair squeezes the opponent, and pressing Y rapidly extends the number of squeeze hits before the opponent is thrown to the other side of Neuro. Probably his best normal attack, since the opponent stays vulnerable to other attacks and status effects during the squeeze.
moves.quote: Pushing Y rapidly can extend how many times an opponent is hit during the squeexing part of the attack. Probably the best out of his normal attacks, especially since it can be easily and readily comboed with a lot of support koma. (deals 15 hits maximum; 5 hits minimum)

moves.name: Up Y
moves.description: Neuro leaps from the ground and attempts to grab an opponent. Best used for ring outs, since it's hard for opponents to recover before getting back up; the lower the area, the better. Can also set opponents up into traveling support koma like Kuwabara's 2-koma.
moves.quote: Up Y: Neuro leaps from the ground and attempts to grab an opponent. Best used for trying to get ring outs, since it's hard for opponents to recover from the move before trying to get back up.

moves.name: Down Y
moves.description: Neuro brings out Yako again, causing her to shoot lasers out of her eyes. Breaks an opponent's guard, like all characters' down Y moves; otherwise not great.
moves.quote: Down Y: Neuro brings out Yako again, and does something that causes her to shoot lasers out of her eyes. Has the property of breaking an opponent's guard, like all characters down Y moves.

moves.name: Aerial Y
moves.description: Neuro slips into his regular form and coughs up one of his 777 Underworld Tools: Evil Friday. Once it hits the ground, it breaks into two eyeballs that crawl the floor in each direction until they hit an opponent/object or a few seconds pass; the eyeballs will not go off a ledge. If an opponent is hit by the ball before it lands, they are stunned for a second or two. A very good move overall, especially in arenas with little to no ledges.
moves.damage: Power/Knowledge: 13 per crawling eye hit; Laughter: 19-20 per crawling eyeball hit
moves.quote: If an opponent is hit the ball before it lands on a platform/arena floor, they will be stunned for a second or two. Very great move all around, particularly in arenas that have little to no other ledges, such as the Dark Tournament Arena.

unresolved: No SELECT Ultimate Action or B-string move is described anywhere in the guide.

The 4-koma (Power) battle koma section repeats the exact same Neutral X ('You, you are the killer!') and Up X ('Ejiki') text, damage, and health (152) as the 4-koma (Knowledge) section verbatim; the guide gives no koma-specific differences between the two 4-koma variants despite listing them as separate entries.

Only one 5-koma variant (Knowledge) is described, even though the evolution chart in section 4 lists '5: 5-koma(battle)' without specifying nature, and the 'Which Battle Koma To Use?' comparison discusses '4 and 5 komas' generally; no 5-koma (Power) entry appears.

Section 5 opens with a note that for Neuro's 4-koma power nature, the knowledge and laughter damage keys should be swapped ('Neuro will cause the most damage to knowledge characters, so switch the knowledge and the laughter damage key for that specific koma'); this note is not reflected anywhere in the per-move damage numbers themselves, which are only labeled Power/Knowledge vs Laughter throughout section 5.
The support koma section (6) does not state a nature for the 2-koma or 3-koma, unlike the battle koma section which specifies nature per koma.
Guide text has typos/garbled spots (e.g. 'Nuetral X', 'thier', 'availible', 'excat', 'sythe', 'radious') left as-is in quotes where directly cited.
